title: Where to Stay in Chitwan: Sauraha, Meghauli or Amaltari
meta_description: Sauraha, Meghauli, Kasara or Amaltari? How to choose a Chitwan base by budget, crowds, wildlife, access and style of stay, with the lodges we use.
summary: Sauraha is the lively, budget-friendly base with the most choice. Meghauli, on the quiet western side, has Chitwan's best high-end lodges and fewer jeeps. Amaltari, further west, is the place for Tharu homestays and Tiger Tops Tharu Lodge. Kasara, near the park headquarters, sits in between. Choose by budget, pace and crowds.

sections.heading: Four bases, four kinds of trip
paras: Chitwan National Park is large, about 953 square kilometres, and where you stay shapes your whole visit. The park's northern boundary runs along the Rapti and Narayani rivers, and almost every lodge sits on the village side of that line, looking across the water into the park. The difference between bases is less about the animals, which move along the whole river, and more about crowds, comfort, price and how easily you can reach the more remote parts of the park.

Most visitors choose between four areas: Sauraha in the east, Kasara and Patihani in the middle, Meghauli in the west, and Amaltari across the Narayani on the Nawalpur side. Each one suits a different traveller, and on longer trips it can make sense to split your nights between two of them.

sections.heading: Sauraha: lively, easy and good value
paras: Sauraha is Chitwan's tourist village, on the north bank of the Rapti about 30 minutes by road from Bharatpur airport and roughly 5 to 7 hours from Kathmandu or 5 hours from Pokhara by road. It grew from a small Tharu settlement into a town of hotels, restaurants, guide offices and cafes, and today it is the base for most Chitwan visitors. The main ticket office for the park, the canoe put-in and the elephant breeding centre at Khorsor are all close by.

The advantages are clear. There is accommodation for every budget, from simple guesthouses to comfortable resorts such as Green Park Chitwan, plenty of places to eat, and easy, affordable activities with shared jeeps, canoes and walks. You can watch rhino from the riverbank at sunset and walk to a Tharu village after dinner. The drawback is crowds: in peak season many jeeps head into the eastern part of the park, and the village can feel busy and commercial.
list: Best for: first-timers, budget and mid-range travellers, short stays, families
Getting there: 30 min from Bharatpur airport; tourist buses from Kathmandu and Pokhara
Stays we use: Green Park Chitwan and selected mid-range hotels

sections.heading: Meghauli: quiet, high-end and wild
paras: Meghauli is a Tharu farming village on the Rapti in the west of the park, about 45 km and an hour and a quarter by road from Bharatpur airport. This was where Nepal's safari tourism began in the 1960s, when guests flew in to a grass strip for Tiger Tops. Today it is home to the park's leading luxury lodges, including Meghauli Serai, A Taj Safari, and Barahi Jungle Lodge, both with views across the river into some of the best rhino grassland in Chitwan.

Far fewer jeeps enter the park from this side, and the western sector feels wilder, with long stretches of forest and grassland and good chances of sloth bear, gaur and, with luck, tiger. Lodges run their own naturalist teams and organise all activities, so you rarely need to think about logistics. The trade-off is price and distance: Meghauli is more expensive and further from the airport, and there is little to do in the village beyond the lodges.
list: Best for: couples, honeymooners, photographers, travellers wanting comfort and quiet
Getting there: about 1 h 15 min by road from Bharatpur airport
Stays we use: Meghauli Serai and Barahi Jungle Lodge

sections.heading: Kasara and Patihani: the middle ground
paras: Kasara is the headquarters of Chitwan National Park and home to the gharial conservation breeding centre, which has raised these critically endangered crocodiles since 1978 for release into Nepal's rivers. The nearby village of Patihani, on the northern edge of the park between Sauraha and Meghauli, has a handful of resorts, including Kasara Resort, which offer a quieter stay than Sauraha with easy access to the central park.

From here you can explore the central lakes and forests, visit the gharial centre and reach Bishazari Tal and Devghat easily. It is a good compromise for travellers who want more comfort and fewer crowds than Sauraha without the full price of Meghauli.

sections.heading: Amaltari: homestays and the western edge
paras: Amaltari lies on the western edge of Chitwan National Park, in Nawalpur district, on the west bank of the Narayani. It is best known for its Tharu community homestay, where village families host guests in rooms built in the Tharu style, and for Tiger Tops Tharu Lodge, designed after the traditional Tharu longhouse, with mud walls and verandahs.

Amaltari has its own park entry point, so jeep safaris and walks go straight into the quieter western sector. The river and wetlands nearby are good for birds, and there is a strong sense of village life. Facilities are simpler than in Meghauli, except at Tiger Tops, and nightlife is non-existent, which is exactly the point for most people who come here.
list: Best for: culture lovers, slow travellers, families wanting a homestay
Getting there: about 1.5 to 2 h by road from Bharatpur airport
Stays we use: Amaltari community homestay and Tiger Tops Tharu Lodge

sections.heading: What lodges include and what they do not
paras: Chitwan lodges sell their rooms in very different ways, and comparing prices only works if you know what is included. Most upscale lodges in Meghauli and Amaltari sell packages with full board, all safari activities, naturalists and sometimes park fees included, which makes a high nightly rate look less steep once you add everything up. In Sauraha, many hotels sell rooms on a bed-and-breakfast or room-only basis, and activities are booked separately, either through the hotel or one of the many guide offices in the village.

Before you book, check whether park entry fees are included, how many activities are offered each day, whether jeeps are shared or private, and who leads the safaris: a lodge naturalist or a freelance guide. Ask about airport transfers too, as Meghauli and Amaltari are a long way from Bharatpur and transfers can add up. Community homestays usually include all meals and a local guide for village walks, while park safaris are arranged as an extra.
Whichever base you choose, booking ahead matters most in October, November and from February to April, when the best rooms in every area fill early.

sections.heading: How long to stay and how to split nights
paras: Two nights is the minimum for any base, and three is better, giving time for a canoe trip, a half-day and a full-day jeep safari, a walk and a village visit. On a four or five-night stay, consider splitting between two bases: for example, two nights in Sauraha for its energy and easy activities, followed by two nights in Meghauli or Amaltari for quiet and the western park. The drive between them is about one to two hours.

If time is short and you are coming from Kathmandu by road, Sauraha is the most convenient. If you are flying in and want comfort, Meghauli is easy from Bharatpur. If you want to understand Tharu life, choose Amaltari or a homestay in Barauli. Whichever base you pick, the river at sunset will look much the same: rhino on the far bank, smoke rising from the villages and the first frogs starting up as the light goes.

faqs.q: Is Sauraha or Meghauli better for a Chitwan safari?
faqs.a: Both give good wildlife viewing. Sauraha is cheaper, livelier and easier to reach, with many hotels and restaurants, but busier in the park. Meghauli is quieter, with high-end lodges, fewer jeeps and access to the wilder western sector. For a budget or first trip, choose Sauraha; for comfort and quiet, choose Meghauli.

faqs.q: Where are the luxury lodges in Chitwan?
faqs.a: Most are in Meghauli, on the western side of the park: Meghauli Serai, A Taj Safari, and Barahi Jungle Lodge. Tiger Tops Tharu Lodge is in Amaltari, further west. Kasara and Patihani have upper mid-range resorts. Sauraha also has comfortable resorts, though fewer at the top end.

faqs.q: Can I stay inside Chitwan National Park?
faqs.a: No. Lodges inside the park were closed in 2012, and all accommodation is now in villages and buffer zone areas outside the park boundary. Many lodges sit right on the river, looking across into the park, so you can often watch wildlife from your terrace.

faqs.q: How far is Sauraha from Bharatpur airport?
faqs.a: About 15 to 20 km, roughly 30 to 40 minutes by road. Most hotels arrange pick-ups. Bharatpur has regular flights from Kathmandu, about 25 minutes. Meghauli is further, about 45 km or an hour and a quarter, and Amaltari about 1.5 to 2 hours depending on the road.

faqs.q: Is Amaltari a good base for wildlife?
faqs.a: Yes. Amaltari has its own park entry point into the western sector, where there are far fewer vehicles than near Sauraha. Rhino, deer, gaur and many birds are seen, and the river and wetlands nearby are good for birding. Choose it if you want wildlife and village life together.

faqs.q: What is the cheapest place to stay in Chitwan?
faqs.a: Sauraha has the widest choice of budget guesthouses and hotels, and activities are cheapest there because you can share jeeps and guides. Community homestays in Amaltari and Barauli are also good value, with meals included. Meghauli is the most expensive area, with mainly upscale lodges.

faqs.q: Should I split my stay between two Chitwan bases?
faqs.a: On stays of four nights or more, it can be a great idea. Two nights in Sauraha for easy activities and village life, then two in Meghauli or Amaltari for the quieter western park, gives you two different sides of Chitwan. The transfer takes about one to two hours by road.

faqs.q: Which Chitwan base is best for families?
faqs.a: Sauraha suits most families, with many hotels, some with pools, easy short activities and plenty of food choices. Amaltari's homestay is a wonderful experience for families happy with simple rooms. Meghauli works for families seeking comfort, but check lodge policies on children's ages for activities.

faqs.q: Which base is best for seeing tigers in Chitwan?
faqs.a: Bases in the west, Meghauli and Amaltari, give quicker access to the quieter parts of the park where tigers are less disturbed, and lodges there run full-day safaris with experienced naturalists. Still, tigers can appear anywhere along the river. More days in the park matter more than the base you choose.
